KEY MESSAGE 1...Periods of rain showers will impact the area into tonight 
for Delmarva and far southern New Jersey.

Massive High pressure well to the north is beginning to push its 
influence southward across the southern Poconos and north NJ this 
afternoon. Clouds are thinning as a North to Northeast flow 
strengthens. The north edge of the steady rains (currently across 
Delmarva and south NJ) continues to slowly push southward. These 
showers will continue tonight before largely ending by
Wednesday as drier air continues to push southward.  

KEY MESSAGE 2...A strengthening surface low off the Eastern Seaboard 
during the middle and latter parts of this week will keep persistent 
northeast to north flow in place through at least Friday. Depending 
on the track of the low, it could bring increased rainfall chances 
and windy conditions to the parts of the region Friday and into the 
weekend.

A mid-level impulse currently traversing portions of the Midwest 
into the Ohio Valley will continue eastward towards the Eastern 
Seaboard tonight into Wednesday. Weak surface cyclogenesis has begun 
off the coast of the Carolinas, with the low expected to continue 
intensifying through late this week. The initial track of the 
developing low is expected to be to the northeast, well offshore. 
However, with a strong high centered over portions of Quebec, a 
sharp pressure gradient over the region will at least lead to breezy 
conditions beginning today through Thursday near the coast. The 
strongest pressure gradient, and thus winds, are forecast to occur 
on Wednesday into Wednesday night. It should remain mostly dry 
during the Wednesday through Thursday period, though some showers 
may linger across Delmarva Wednesday morning.

Given a consistent forecast for sustained winds 25-35 mph along the 
Atlantic coasts of New Jersey and Delaware on Wednesday, a Wind 
Advisory will be in effect for the immediate coastal strip from 6 AM 
Wednesday through midnight Wednesday night. Some gusts near 45 mph 
are also possible.

For late this week into this weekend, model guidance remains largely 
split into two camps. One camp allows the low to continue to track 
northeastward away from the region, and the other camp features a 
westward deviation of the low, or even additional surface 
cyclogenesis closer to the coast. Given these factors, uncertainty 
for Friday and beyond remains quite high, with a large range of 
potential outcomes. The deterministic EC and all of its ensembles 
continue to feature the scenario that would lead to greater impacts. 
The deterministic GFS remains far enough out to sea to keep impacts 
confined to the immediate coast with gusty winds and minimal 
rainfall. However, it should be noted that the GFS has trended 
westward somewhat this afternoon, and a few GEFS members feature 
solutions fairly similar to the EC. It is unclear whether this is a 
single-run deviation or the beginning of the development of better 
model consensus. For now feature PoPs in the 20-40% range along the 
coast Friday, expanding inland to the I-95 corridor Saturday and 
areawide Saturday night into Sunday. Regardless of which scenario 
pans out, precipitation chances and winds will be highest close to 
the coast and decrease with inland extent. 

Sunday night into Monday, regardless of which scenario ultimately 
pans out, the low will begin to track away from the area, allowing 
rain chances to decrease and winds to subside. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...Multiple rounds of significant tidal flooding expected for 
this week. Coastal Flood Warnings and Advisories issued.

With a slow moving coastal storm expected, the threat for tidal
flooding has increased. Strong onshore flow that is projected 
to last for several days will result in water piling up across 
tidal tributaries and within back bays of coastal communities. 
Tidal levels will also be enhanced with astronomical tides 
increasing with the upcoming Full Moon on Saturday. This 
combination of factors will lead to widespread tidal flooding, 
some of which is expected to get to the Moderate stage. While 
not currently forecast, the threat for major flooding is not off
the table, especially getting near the full moon. 

Minor tidal flooding begins with this afternoon and evening's
high tide cycle. The Coastal Flood Advisory for tonight was 
expanded to include New Castle County in Delaware and Salem 
County in New Jersey as northeasterly winds keep water piling in
the Delaware Bay. 

The Advisory remains in effect for Ocean, Atlantic, and Cape 
May County in New Jersey and Kent and Sussex County in Delaware 
as well. For these same areas, tide levels are expected to 
increase for Wednesday and Thursday, and are expected to get to
Moderate stage. The Coastal Flood Watch was upgraded to a
Coastal Flood Warning for Wednesday and Thursday evening's high
tide. Moderate tidal flooding could even continue into the 
weekend. As mentioned above, cannot rule out tide levels
